subject: Clarify egress & SIEM export constraints for private deployment
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: secops@finco.com, acme-cloud-support@acmecloud.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify egress & SIEM export constraints for private deployment

Hi team,

We kicked off the FinCo private deployment runbook last week and have a couple of open questions about telemetry egress and SIEM integration that will block the on-site install next Wed. Wanted to capture them here so we can get aligned before dry-run.

Ask summary (short):
- What egress endpoints/ports are allowed from the FinCo VPC to Redwood-managed collectors?
- Do you require syslog over TLS (RFC 5425), Splunk HEC with mTLS, or an OTLP pull model behind a private link?
- Any retention or sampling constraints we should bake into the Otel collector config?

Notes/context: we prefer pushing via an in-customer forwarder (OpenTelemetry Collector) to Redwood's private onramp. Options we've prepared:
- Syslog TLS -> customer Splunk HEC syslog forwarder (default TCP/6514)
- OTLP/gRPC -> Redwood egress gateway (mTLS + client cert rotated daily)
- HEC -> direct Splunk HEC endpoint with bearer token + IP allowlist

Attached: export-config-sample.yaml (OTel collector + batching settings), network-egress-sketch.png (rough sketch of NAT/eBPF hops).

If you can reply with the allowed outbound CIDR(s), firewall ports, and preferred transport, we can lock the collector settings and provide the proof bundle for the compliance review.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Tech Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

----
From: secops@finco.com
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify egress & SIEM export constraints for private deployment

Dylan,

Thanks for the summary. A few items from FinCo SecOps:

1) Egress CIDRs: we allow outbound to our vendor peer space only; vendor endpoints must be behind the FinCo peering service. For this install we can temporarily open the following /27 to the vendor peer: 10.240.32.0/27 (only for the collector egress subnet).

2) Transport preference: we prefer OTLP/gRPC over mTLS-enabled private link. The reasons: consistent tracing context, payload compression, and easier sampling controls. HEC + bearer tokens are acceptable only if the vendor cannot peer.

3) Ports: allow outbound 4317 (OTLP gRPC), 443 for control-plane, and 6514 only for legacy syslog fallbacks.

4) Retention/sampling: we require sampling at the collector to cap trace ingestion to ~10k traces/day for the initial 30-day trial. Metrics/logs retention will be managed on Redwood side but FinCo requires proof that PII/secret fields are redacted before egress.

5) Mutual auth/keys: client certs rotated daily via our signing service; vendor must accept JWT-based short-lived tokens if cert rotation is not possible during PoC.

Can you produce a new collector config with: OTLP exporter, batch_size 512, compression: gzip, resource attributes: service.name + env, and a scrubber processor config to redact PII keys (email, ssn, card_number) prior to egress? Also provide the steps for cert rotation or token exchange.

Regards,
FinCo SecOps

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: FinCo SecOps <secops@finco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify egress & SIEM export constraints for private deployment

Hi all,

Appreciate the specificity — that's helpful. I sketched a minimal collector config that matches the ask and attached a redacted example inline below. This is meant to be the PoC config; we will iterate for scale.

Collector snippets (inline):
- receivers: otlp (gRPC) on 4317 (local/sidecar)
- processors: batch (send_interval: 5s, send_batch_size: 512), attributes (action: delete for keys: password, ssn, card_number), resource/normalize
- exporters: otlp (endpoint: https://10.240.32.5:4317, tls: {insecure: false, cert_file: /etc/collector/client.crt, key_file: /etc/collector/client.key, ca_file: /etc/collector/finco-ca.crt}, compression: gzip)

Operational notes:
- Certificate rotation: we can automate reload via SIGHUP and use a small sidecar that pulls daily certs from the FinCo signer endpoint. If FinCo prefers JWT short-lived tokens instead, we can swap exporter config to use headers: Authorization: Bearer <token> and rotate tokens via the same sidecar.
- Firewall: collector egress to 10.240.32.5:4317 (peer) only; all other outbound is denied.
- Trace sampling: implement probabilistic sampling at incoming pipeline with target rate 0.005 (0.5%) initially to match the 10k/day cap; we can wire an adaptive tail-sampler once we confirm service qps.

I've attached the full YAML in export-config-sample.yaml for your review.

Next steps (action items):
- FinCo to confirm the peer IP and CA bundle for mTLS (secops).
- Dylan to validate network diagram and NAT rules with on-site infra.
- Kimberly to prepare compliance checklist and redaction proof artifact for audit.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCo SecOps <secops@finco.com>, acme-cloud-support@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify egress & SIEM export constraints for private deployment

Got it — thanks everyone. Quick summary and immediate asks so we can lock the dry-run: 

1) Protocol: OTLP/gRPC (4317) with mTLS preferred, fallback to bearer-token HEC if peering proves problematic.
2) Egress CIDR: FinCo will provision 10.240.32.0/27 peer; we will target 10.240.32.5 as the collector endpoint in the PoC config.
3) Collector config: Marissa will drop updated export-config-sample.yaml into the Drive folder (link below) with the scrubber config and sampling set to 0.5%.
4) Cert rotation: FinCo to share signer endpoint and CA bundle; if unavailable we'll use short-lived JWTs.
5) Compliance: Kimberly — can you produce the redaction proof artifact (sample input -> redacted output) by Tue EOD?

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyzShared/telemetry-handbook (export-config-sample.yaml v1.2)

I'll block a 30-min dry-run call for Wed 10:00 PT and ping onsite infra to confirm NAT rules. If anyone needs to push changes earlier, reply-all.

Regards,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Tech Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
